text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High 5xx rate from Hosted API (us-east-1) observed 2026-03-15T09:12Z. Route: /v1/generate. 5m avg 5xx = 12%, baseline < 0.5%. Pager: @Alex W (oncall).

Alex W: oncall ack. looking at graphs now. opening timeline and attaching logs here.

PagerDuty: Incident created and paged: oncall -> Alex W. Severity: P1 (customer-facing errors).

Alex W: quick check — traffic spike corresponds with tonight's canary roll (model-service: my-model v1.3.7). Canary target 5% traffic.

Maria G: thanks — I'm free to help with diffs and log scraping. Isolate canary pods?

Alex W: yes. pulled logs from canary pod group. something odd in tokenizer init time and repeated OOM-ish traces (not full OOM). logs excerpt:

```
2026-03-15T09:11:44Z inference-canary-1 my-model v1.3.7 INFO starting kv-cache warmup
2026-03-15T09:11:45Z inference-canary-1 my-model v1.3.7 WARN kv-cache miss burst=120
2026-03-15T09:11:46Z inference-canary-1 my-model v1.3.7 ERROR runtime: failed allocate 134217728 bytes: transient retry
2026-03-15T09:11:47Z inference-canary-1 my-model v1.3.7 ERROR handler: request_id=abc123 status=502 err="upstream runtime failure"
2026-03-15T09:11:50Z inference-canary-2 my-model v1.3.7 INFO request handled latency=2434ms
```

Sanjay P: that ERROR looks like a memory allocation retry path in the new quant kernel. v1.3.7 had a kernel bump last night. pulling canary diffs.

Alex W: paste of model package diffs (sha hashes redacted):

```
--- v1.3.6/package.json
+++ v1.3.7/package.json
@@
-  "inference_kernel": "kern-a-1.2.0",
+  "inference_kernel": "kern-a-1.3.0",
-  "tokenizer": {
-    "merge_rules": 1024
-  }
+  "tokenizer": {
+    "merge_rules": 2048
+  }
```

Maria G: interesting — tokenizer changes could increase memory pressure for long prompts. Also kernel bump may change allocator behavior. Any per-route config change?

Alex W: per-route config unchanged. Canary traffic sample payloads match prod. We see success rate drop only for the canary pods (v1.3.7). Hosted (v1.3.6) healthy.

Eva L: customer impact check: which customers hit canary? Dedicated and enterprise customers pinned to v1.3.6; only hosted free-tier and some new accounts got routed to canary 5% — estimated affected requests ~800/min. No SLA customers impacted yet.

Chris R: that's good. propose immediate action: stop canary rollout and pin routing back to v1.3.6 globally for safety. rollback can be done two ways: (A) rollback rollout controller to v1.3.6 (fast) or (B) adjust router policy to exclude v1.3.7. A is preferred.

Alex W: agree. initiating rollback now. running command:

```
# force-roll back model rollout to previous stable version
rwctl rollout set my-model --version 1.3.6 --force
```

IncidentBot: Command executed by Alex W at 2026-03-15T09:18Z: rwctl rollout set my-model --version 1.3.6 --force

Alex W: saw immediate drop in canary pods traffic. monitoring metrics.

(1m later)

Alex W: 5xx rate on /v1/generate dropped from 12% -> 0.6% in us-east-1 within 90s. latencies trending back to baseline. :white_check_mark:

Maria G: can we pin the new change in the model registry to prevent auto-rollouts until we understand root cause?

Sanjay P: yes — adding tag `hold-investigate` and pinning.

```
# pin version in deployment config
rwctl model pin my-model --version 1.3.6 --reason "canary regression 2026-03-15"
```

Alex W: done. IncidentBot: model my-model pinned to 1.3.6 by Alex W at 2026-03-15T09:22Z.

Eva L: customer comms — notifying developer mailing list and users who hit canary with a short note. I'll draft a blurb after we confirm RCA.

Chris R: quick hypothesis tracker in-thread:
- H1: kernel 1.3.0 allocator regression under specific tokenization patterns -> memory allocation retry -> 502s
- H2: tokenizer merge_rules change increased memory per request causing kv-cache thrash
- H3: config drift in canary runtime (env var) causing degraded performance (low prob)

Maria G: action items:
- capture full canary pod heap and allocator logs from 09:10-09:20 (Sanjay)
- run reproduce with long prompt payloads locally against kernel 1.3.0 (Maria + Alex)
- diff runtime env and start flags between v1.3.6 and v1.3.7 pods (Eva)
- check router logs for misrouted traffic (Chris)

Sanjay P: started collection: `kubectl cp` of /var/log/allocator from inference-canary-* to staging bucket. ETA 10m.

Alex W: adding timeline notes here:
- 09:11Z canary rollout started -> v1.3.7 (5% traffic)
- 09:12Z metrics alert: 5xx spike
- 09:14Z first page to oncall (Alex)
- 09:18Z rollback to v1.3.6 executed
- 09:20Z 5xx back to baseline

Maria G: good timeline. I'll start perf repro now. leaving notes in /eng-ml/rollouts.

(15m later)

Sanjay P: allocator traces show repeated transient allocation retries around 128MB boundary then success after several retries. pattern not present in v1.3.6 traces. grabbing core dumps for deeper analysis.

Chris R: router logs show canary routing was correct, no misrouting.

Alex W: recommending postmortem path: immediate RCA to focus on kernel allocator change + tokenizer memory characteristics. classify incident as P1 (but limited customer impact). Proposal: block kernel 1.3.0 in release pipeline until kernel team signs off.

Maria G: agreed. will open a release-block PR and add failing test to canary harness to catch allocation retry pattern.

Eva L: drafted customer message: "We rolled back a canary model update after a small subset of requests experienced increased errors. No dedicated customers affected. We're investigating and will follow up with root cause." Will send after RCA draft.

Alex W: marking incident as resolved for paging. moving to RCA coordination channel. please add any residual artifacts below and tag owners. :eyes:

IncidentBot: Incident P1-2026-03-15-001 automatically transitioned to POSTMORTEM at 2026-03-15T09:45Z by Alex W.

Chris R: notes saved to /incidents/2026-03-15-canary-regression-logbundle.tar.gz (S3). folks: leave thumbs up when you have confirmed your action items. :thumbsup:
